findings.body: The background legacy write receives a canceled context and is aborted, leaving legacy storage unsynchronized despite the unified write succeeding.
findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
findings.failure_mode: Best-effort replication is canceled precisely when it needs to continue after the response.
findings.impact: The background legacy write receives a canceled context and is aborted, leaving legacy storage unsynchronized despite the unified write succeeding.
findings.root_cause: The asynchronous replication goroutine inherits the lifecycle of the synchronous request.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the background operation context from a non-request parent (while explicitly propagating any required values/logging) and apply the 10-second timeout to that context.
findings.title: Do not derive asynchronous legacy writes from the request context
findings.trigger: A Mode 3 write returns to an HTTP client before the legacy operation finishes; request contexts are canceled when the request completes or the client disconnects.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R51 shows ctx derived from request context with WithTimeoutCause. When HTTP request completes/client disconnects, parent ctx cancels, causing the goroutine's derived ctx to also cancel before the 10s timeout, aborting the legacy write. This is a real defect in async replication design.

findings.body: The callback is evaluated a second time against the legacy object's state, so legacy can receive a different update or fail while unified has already accepted the update.
findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
findings.failure_mode: The two stores apply different logical updates for one client request.
findings.impact: The callback is evaluated a second time against the legacy object's state, so legacy can receive a different update or fail while unified has already accepted the update.
findings.root_cause: The original state-dependent `UpdatedObjectInfo` is reused after unified storage has already resolved the update.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap `objInfo` with an `updateWrapper` containing the successful unified result (preferably a deep copy) before invoking `Legacy.Update`, as the previous implementation did.
findings.title: Replay the resolved update object to legacy storage
findings.trigger: An update callback derives its result from the existing object and unified and legacy versions differ, which is expected while migrating or after a missed asynchronous write.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R139 shows d.Legacy.Update called with raw objInfo instead of updateWrapper containing resolved unified result. The old code (L101-104) wrapped with updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}. Now objInfo.UpdatedObject will re-evaluate against legacy's different state, causing divergent updates.

findings.body: Monitoring reports a legacy-create failure and omits the unified-storage failure/latency even though legacy was never called, misleading failure alerts and migration diagnostics.
findings.failure_mode: Operational metrics attribute failures to the wrong backend.
findings.impact: Monitoring reports a legacy-create failure and omits the unified-storage failure/latency even though legacy was never called, misleading failure alerts and migration diagnostics.
findings.root_cause: The storage error path invokes the legacy duration recorder.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` in this branch.
findings.title: Record create failures against the storage metric
findings.verifier_reason: Line R45 shows d.recordLegacyDuration called when Storage.Create fails. This records a legacy metric for a storage failure - the wrong metric recorder is used. Should be recordStorageDuration as the suggested fix states.

findings.body: The `kind` label of the storage histogram receives every object name, creating unbounded Prometheus time-series cardinality and preventing aggregation by resource kind.
findings.failure_mode: Metrics consume unnecessary memory/cardinality and report incorrectly partitioned delete durations.
findings.impact: The `kind` label of the storage histogram receives every object name, creating unbounded Prometheus time-series cardinality and preventing aggregation by resource kind.
findings.root_cause: The delete success path supplies `name` where the metric API expects a resource kind.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `options.Kind` as the third argument, matching the error path and the metric's `kind` label definition.
findings.title: Use the resource kind rather than object name as the delete metric label
findings.trigger: Mode 3 successfully deletes many objects with distinct names.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R106 shows d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where 'name' is the object name, not options.Kind. The metric's 'kind' label receives unbounded object names instead of resource kind, causing cardinality explosion. Compare to R103 which correctly uses options.Kind.

findings.body: Legacy delete-collection duration and failures are not observable; instead a second, misleading storage duration is emitted after the storage operation already succeeded.
findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
findings.failure_mode: Delete-collection telemetry attributes legacy work to unified storage.
findings.impact: Legacy delete-collection duration and failures are not observable; instead a second, misleading storage duration is emitted after the storage operation already succeeded.
findings.root_cause: The legacy replication goroutine invokes the storage metric recorder.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.
findings.title: Record asynchronous delete-collection replication in the legacy metric
findings.trigger: The asynchronous `Legacy.DeleteCollection` succeeds, fails, or times out.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R166 shows d.recordStorageDuration called in the legacy replication goroutine for DeleteCollection. Should be recordLegacyDuration since this measures legacy operation. This is distinct from candidates 6/7 which are about error paths using wrong recorder.

pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Mode 3 will work the following way:

reads (get, list) : only use unified storage
writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) : write to unified storage and then asynchronously, write to legacy, just as a safe measure.

**Why do we need this feature?**

[Add a description of the problem the feature is trying to solve.]

**Who is this feature for?**

[Add information on what kind of user the feature is for.]

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/search-and-storage-team/issues/53

validated_findings.trigger: Two successful writes for the same object occur close together while the first legacy operation is delayed, such as a create followed immediately by an update or delete.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R50 shows 'go func()' spawning independent goroutines for each mutation. Without serialization per object key, concurrent mutations on the same object can execute out of order in legacy storage, causing divergence. This is a distinct systemic issue from context cancellation.

validated_findings.body: Each request retains a goroutine and its captured objects/options for up to ten seconds, so write traffic above legacy throughput can cause unbounded goroutine and memory growth.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A degraded legacy store can exhaust process resources even though unified writes continue to succeed.
validated_findings.impact: Each request retains a goroutine and its captured objects/options for up to ten seconds, so write traffic above legacy throughput can cause unbounded goroutine and memory growth.
validated_findings.root_cause: The replication path has no concurrency or queue bound.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a bounded replication queue and worker pool with an explicit overload/drop policy and metrics.
validated_findings.title: Bound asynchronous replication work instead of spawning one goroutine per write
validated_findings.trigger: Legacy storage is slow or unavailable while Mode 3 receives sustained create, update, delete, or delete-collection traffic.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R50 shows unbounded goroutine spawning per write with 10s timeout. Under sustained load with slow legacy storage, goroutines accumulate without bound. This is a distinct resource exhaustion concern from ordering issues.

validated_findings.body: The callback is evaluated a second time against the legacy object's state, so legacy can receive a different update or fail while unified has already accepted the update.
validated_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
validated_findings.failure_mode: The two stores apply different logical updates for one client request.
validated_findings.impact: The callback is evaluated a second time against the legacy object's state, so legacy can receive a different update or fail while unified has already accepted the update.
validated_findings.root_cause: The original state-dependent `UpdatedObjectInfo` is reused after unified storage has already resolved the update.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap `objInfo` with an `updateWrapper` containing the successful unified result (preferably a deep copy) before invoking `Legacy.Update`, as the previous implementation did.
validated_findings.title: Replay the resolved update object to legacy storage
validated_findings.trigger: An update callback derives its result from the existing object and unified and legacy versions differ, which is expected while migrating or after a missed asynchronous write.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R139 shows d.Legacy.Update called with raw objInfo instead of updateWrapper containing resolved unified result. The old code (L101-104) wrapped with updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}. Now objInfo.UpdatedObject will re-evaluate against legacy's different state, causing divergent updates.

validated_findings.body: The method returns before scheduling the legacy delete, leaving the stale legacy object permanently present while unified reads report NotFound.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Delete requests cannot repair a stale legacy replica.
validated_findings.impact: The method returns before scheduling the legacy delete, leaving the stale legacy object permanently present while unified reads report NotFound.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new early-return branch treats a unified NotFound the same as an operational failure.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the prior `apierrors.IsNotFound` handling: return early only for non-NotFound unified errors and schedule the legacy delete for a NotFound result.
validated_findings.title: Continue legacy deletion when unified deletion is NotFound
validated_findings.trigger: A delete targets an object that is absent from unified storage but still present in legacy storage, for example after an earlier asynchronous replication failure.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that Delete returns early without scheduling legacy delete on NotFound is incorrect. Looking at R100-116, the code only returns early on err != nil (R101-104), then schedules legacy delete in goroutine (R108-114). There's no special NotFound handling that skips legacy delete - the goroutine always runs on success.

validated_findings.body: Monitoring reports a legacy-create failure and omits the unified-storage failure/latency even though legacy was never called, misleading failure alerts and migration diagnostics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Operational metrics attribute failures to the wrong backend.
validated_findings.impact: Monitoring reports a legacy-create failure and omits the unified-storage failure/latency even though legacy was never called, misleading failure alerts and migration diagnostics.
validated_findings.root_cause: The storage error path invokes the legacy duration recorder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Call `recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` in this branch.
validated_findings.title: Record create failures against the storage metric
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R45 shows d.recordLegacyDuration called when Storage.Create fails. This records a legacy metric for a storage failure - the wrong metric recorder is used. Should be recordStorageDuration as the suggested fix states.

validated_findings.body: Unified update failures are exported as legacy failures, and no corresponding storage error duration is recorded.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Update health metrics misidentify the failing datastore.
validated_findings.impact: Unified update failures are exported as legacy failures, and no corresponding storage error duration is recorded.
validated_findings.root_cause: The unified-storage error branch invokes the legacy metric recorder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace this call with `recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.
validated_findings.title: Record update failures against the storage metric
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R129 shows same pattern as candidate 6 - d.recordLegacyDuration called for Storage.Update failure. Same root cause (wrong metric recorder on storage error path), same fix needed. Merging into candidate 6 as canonical.

validated_findings.body: The `kind` label of the storage histogram receives every object name, creating unbounded Prometheus time-series cardinality and preventing aggregation by resource kind.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Metrics consume unnecessary memory/cardinality and report incorrectly partitioned delete durations.
validated_findings.impact: The `kind` label of the storage histogram receives every object name, creating unbounded Prometheus time-series cardinality and preventing aggregation by resource kind.
validated_findings.root_cause: The delete success path supplies `name` where the metric API expects a resource kind.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `options.Kind` as the third argument, matching the error path and the metric's `kind` label definition.
validated_findings.title: Use the resource kind rather than object name as the delete metric label
validated_findings.trigger: Mode 3 successfully deletes many objects with distinct names.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R106 shows d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where 'name' is the object name, not options.Kind. The metric's 'kind' label receives unbounded object names instead of resource kind, causing cardinality explosion. Compare to R103 which correctly uses options.Kind.

validated_findings.body: Legacy delete-collection duration and failures are not observable; instead a second, misleading storage duration is emitted after the storage operation already succeeded.
validated_findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Delete-collection telemetry attributes legacy work to unified storage.
validated_findings.impact: Legacy delete-collection duration and failures are not observable; instead a second, misleading storage duration is emitted after the storage operation already succeeded.
validated_findings.root_cause: The legacy replication goroutine invokes the storage metric recorder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.
validated_findings.title: Record asynchronous delete-collection replication in the legacy metric
validated_findings.trigger: The asynchronous `Legacy.DeleteCollection` succeeds, fails, or times out.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R166 shows d.recordStorageDuration called in the legacy replication goroutine for DeleteCollection. Should be recordLegacyDuration since this measures legacy operation. This is distinct from candidates 6/7 which are about error paths using wrong recorder.

validated_findings.body: The test still passes because it returns immediately after the unified write and never waits for the goroutine or calls `AssertExpectations`, so it does not verify the newly required legacy replication.
validated_findings.evidence: m.On("Create", mock.Anything, input, mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(exampleObj, nil)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Replication regressions are silently accepted by the Mode 3 test suite.
validated_findings.impact: The test still passes because it returns immediately after the unified write and never waits for the goroutine or calls `AssertExpectations`, so it does not verify the newly required legacy replication.
validated_findings.root_cause: New tests configure mock expectations for asynchronous calls but treat the synchronous API return as completion.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make the legacy mock signal completion, wait for that signal with a bounded timeout, and call `m.AssertExpectations(t)`; apply the same pattern to create, update, delete, and delete-collection tests.
validated_findings.title: Wait for and assert asynchronous legacy replication in Mode 3 tests
validated_findings.trigger: A regression prevents the Mode 3 create goroutine from reaching `Legacy.Create`, such as immediate request-context cancellation or an early return.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R31 shows mock expectation for legacy Create, but the test at R63-77 calls dw.Create and returns without waiting for the async goroutine or calling AssertExpectations. The legacy mock expectation is never verified, so regressions in async replication go undetected.

validated_findings.body: `SetDualWritingMode` only transitions between Modes 1 and 2, so the added case continues running the persisted/default mode rather than Mode 3; it gives no integration coverage of the new behavior and deployments cannot promote through the desired Mode 3 setting.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The test name and configuration claim Mode 3 coverage while execution uses another mode.
validated_findings.impact: `SetDualWritingMode` only transitions between Modes 1 and 2, so the added case continues running the persisted/default mode rather than Mode 3; it gives no integration coverage of the new behavior and deployments cannot promote through the desired Mode 3 setting.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch adds a desired Mode 3 configuration without extending the mode-transition state machine that chooses the actual mode.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add the required transitions to `SetDualWritingMode` for desired Mode 3 (including the supported source modes), then assert `dw.Mode() == Mode3` in the integration setup.
validated_findings.title: Make the added Mode 3 integration case actually select Mode 3
validated_findings.trigger: The helper starts with an unset, Mode 1, or Mode 2 persisted dual-writer mode and this test requests Mode 3.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim requires examining SetDualWritingMode logic. Looking at dualwriter.go L199-218, transitions only handle Mode1<->Mode2. However, the test at R132-144 just passes Mode3 to the helper - whether it actually runs Mode3 depends on SetDualWritingMode implementation which may fall through to default. The finding speculates about state machine behavior without proving the test doesn't work.
